key_insight: An automated image-analysis framework quantified lung adenocarcinoma biomarkers and reproduced prognostic stratification comparable to expert visual scoring.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support more reproducible prognostic research in lung adenocarcinoma, but does not establish treatment-selection or drug-discovery utility.
method: Segment tissue regions using machine learning in an open-source Fiji/ImageJ pipeline.
Calculate tumour-area-weighted Marker Expression Level (MEL) scores with staining normalization.
Combine BRCA1, GLUT1 and QKI MEL scores with tumour stage in a Cox-based prognostic index.
evidence_signal: In 128 patients, MEL correlated with visual H-scores (Spearman ρ = 0.61–0.69; p < 0.001), and the combined index separated disease-free and overall survival risk groups (p < 0.05).
watch_item: Independent external validation is not described in the abstract, and segmentation performed less well in highly immune-infiltrated stromal regions.
paper_title: Development and Validation of an Automated Image-Based Method for Prognostic Stratification in Lung Adenocarcinoma using Immunohistochemical Markers
